name: Syndromic Genetic Ectopia Lentis

criteria.description: Presence of lens dislocation (ectopia lentis) confirmed by ophthalmological examination
Presence of systemic features consistent with connective tissue disorder (e.g., skeletal abnormalities, cardiovascular involvement)
Identification of pathogenic variant in genes associated with syndromic ectopia lentis (e.g., FBN1, ADAMTSL4)
Positive family history of ectopia lentis or related connective tissue disorders

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of ectopia lentis plus at least one systemic feature consistent with connective tissue disorder
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; clinical diagnosis relies on ocular and systemic findings.

searchTerms: lens out of place in eye

pathognomonic.notes: Long limbs and fingers characteristic of connective tissue involvement
searchTerms: marfanoid body type with long fingers
tall thin build with spider-like fingers
long limbs and fingers resembling Marfan syndrome

common.notes: Common cardiac manifestation in syndromic ectopia lentis
Increased range of motion in multiple joints

occasional.notes: May progress to aneurysm if untreated

rare.notes: Due to connective tissue fragility in lungs
Widening of the dural sac around the spinal cord

laboratory: Genetic testing revealing pathogenic variants in FBN1, ADAMTSL4, or related genes
imaging: Echocardiography showing mitral valve prolapse and aortic root dilation
Ocular ultrasound or slit-lamp examination confirming lens dislocation
genetic: Mutations in ADAMTSL4 gene (isolated ectopia lentis syndrome)
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Physical examination revealing marfanoid features and joint hypermobility

distinguishingFeatures: Systemic features overlap but Marfan syndrome has more prominent cardiovascular complications
Presence of FBN1 mutations with broader phenotype
Lens dislocation typically inferonasal rather than superotemporal
Elevated homocysteine levels and metabolic abnormalities
Short stature and brachydactyly contrasting with marfanoid habitus

redFlags: Sudden vision loss indicating possible retinal detachment
Chest pain or shortness of breath suggesting aortic dissection
Progressive aortic root dilation on imaging
references: Loeys BL, Dietz HC. Marfan Syndrome and Related Disorders: 2014 Update. Curr Opin Pediatr. 2014.
Khan AO. Ectopia Lentis: Clinical Features and Genetic Causes. Saudi J Ophthalmol. 2016.
Orphanet: Syndromic Genetic Ectopia Lentis. Orphanet Report Series. 2023.
